query: Where does opening a web link fall back to Python's built-in browser launcher when the desktop opener program can't be started on Linux?
why: _termui_impl.py:824-841 (xdg-open OSError -> webbrowser.open for http/https when not locate/wait)

query: When an unknown subcommand name is typed, where does it retry the lookup after normalizing the token, and re-parse the arguments if the unrecognized word looks like a flag so a help request still reaches the parent?
why: core.py:2011-2028 (token_normalize_func retry; _split_opt -> parse_args before NoSuchCommand)

query: Under what circumstances does an option whose value may be omitted refuse to take the next command-line token as its value because that token looks like the start of another option?
why: parser.py:453-465 (_flag_needs_value and next arg starts with an opt prefix -> FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE)

query: When a filesystem path argument points at something that doesn't exist, where is it accepted and returned without further checks as long as existence wasn't required?
why: types.py:1113-1117 (os.stat OSError -> if not self.exists: return coerce_path_result)

query: In zsh tab-completion output, when are colons inside a completion value backslash-escaped, and when are they left alone?
why: shell_completion.py:407-419 (escape ':' only if item has help text, i.e. help != sentinel)

query: If looking up the installed version by package name fails, where does it try to map the import name to the distribution that provides it, and error out when several distributions match?
why: decorators.py:505-528 (PackageNotFoundError -> packages_distributions(); 1 match -> use it, >1 -> RuntimeError)

query: When an on/off switch option has to be asked for interactively, where does it switch to a yes/no question instead of free-text entry and force a non-boolean default into true or false?
why: core.py:3347-3364 (is_bool_flag -> default coerced with bool(); return confirm(...))

query: For safe whole-file replacement writes, where is a randomly named hidden scratch file created next to the target, retried on name collisions, and given the original file's permission bits?
why: _compat.py:414-449 (os.stat perm; loop with random .__atomic-write name, O_EXCL, retry on EEXIST; os.chmod perm; wrap in _AtomicFile)

query: Where does the external-editor flow push the scratch file's modification time a couple of seconds into the past so it can tell afterwards whether the user actually saved?
why: _termui_impl.py:747-760 (os.utime mtime - 2; compare getmtime after edit; return None if unchanged)

query: When a file-typed argument turns out to be a standard stream, where is only a flush (not a close) registered to run when the command finishes?
why: types.py:948-962 (open_stream should_close False -> ctx.call_on_close(safecall(f.flush)))

query: Where does an error object snapshot the color preference at creation time, because the active invocation context may be gone by the time the message is printed?
why: exceptions.py:44-49 (self.show_color = resolve_color_default() cached for show())

query: When simulating a command run with environment overrides, where does an override with no value delete the variable, and where are the original environment values put back afterwards?
why: testing.py:564-583 (value None -> del os.environ[key]; finally restores old_env)

query: Where are other parameters that have not been given a value yet temporarily shown as None to a user callback, and then switched back to the unset marker once the callback returns?
why: core.py:2569-2594 (unset_keys -> ctx.params.update None; callback; restore UNSET where still None)

query: On Unix, where does raw single-key input open the controlling terminal device directly when standard input is redirected, and restore the terminal settings afterwards?
why: _termui_impl.py:910-931 (not isatty(stdin) -> open('/dev/tty'); tcsetattr restore; close f)

query: How is a long help text shortened to a one-line summary so that it stops right after the first sentence-ending period without adding an ellipsis, and otherwise trims whole words and appends dots?
why: utils.py:65-111 (first paragraph only; word ending in '.' -> return without '...'; else drop words to fit + '...')

query: In a cluster of single-letter flags glued together, where does the remainder of the cluster become the value of the first letter that needs one?
why: parser.py:407-413 (option.takes_value and chars left -> state.rargs.insert(0, arg[i:]); stop)

query: How is the time-remaining estimate smoothed: where does it keep a rolling window of the most recent per-item timings and recompute them at most about once a second?
why: _termui_impl.py:302-322 (skip if <1.0s since last_eta; step=elapsed/pos; self.avg = self.avg[-6:] + [step])

query: When an option that can be repeated and takes several values per use is read from an environment variable, where is the string split and then grouped into fixed-size tuples?
why: core.py:3440-3447 (value_depth>0 -> split_envvar_value; multiple and nargs!=1 -> batch(multi_rv, nargs))

query: When several spellings of the same option are listed together in help output, how are they ordered so that the ones with shorter prefixes come first?
why: formatting.py:311-320 (collect (len(prefix), opt); sort by prefix length; join with ', ')

query: Where does a yes/no question build its hint so that the letter of the default answer is capitalized, and show both letters lowercase when there is no default?
why: termui.py:274-279 (default None -> 'y/n', True -> 'Y/n', False -> 'y/N')

query: When unpacking positional arguments against a list of expected counts that includes one slot marked to soak up everything left over, where is that slot filled with all the remaining input while the items declared after it are collected from the tail end and then put back in their original order?
why: parser.py:51-108. nargs<0 records spos=len(rv) and appends a placeholder (94-99); after the loop, rv[spos] is set to the remaining args and everything after the wildcard slot, which was popped from the right, is reversed back into forward order (103-106).

query: In the fish shell's completion output, where are newline characters escaped and tab characters swapped for spaces inside a completion item's help text before it is written out?
why: shell_completion.py:442-456. When item.help is set, '\n' is replaced with the literal two-character sequence and '\t' with a space (452-453) before formatting the type,value\thelp line.

query: For a numeric option restricted to a range, where is a value outside the minimum or maximum pulled back to the nearest boundary instead of raising an error when that lenient mode is turned on?
why: types.py:608-639. After computing lt_min/gt_max, if self.clamp is true the value is replaced via self._clamp(min, 1, min_open) or self._clamp(max, -1, max_open) (623-628) before the ordinary out-of-range failure would otherwise be raised.

query: Where is a short piece of text such as 'yes', 'on' or '1' turned into a true or false Python value by trimming whitespace, lowercasing it, and looking it up in a fixed table of recognized spellings?
why: types.py:797-810. Non-bool input is stripped and lower-cased, then looked up in the bool_states mapping (defined 764-779); returns None if nothing matches.

query: When rewrapping a multi-paragraph block of help text, where does a paragraph that begins with a special no-rewrap marker get passed through untouched instead of being re-flowed, while its leading indentation is still measured and reapplied?
why: formatting.py:31-107. Paragraph buffering (74-97) checks if the first line of a paragraph is the backspace marker '\b' and, if so, joins the rest with newlines untouched (81-82); the render loop later calls indent_only instead of fill for that paragraph (100-104).

query: When printing a two-column list of terms and their descriptions, where does a term too long to fit the first column push its description down onto its own line instead of sharing the row with the term?
why: formatting.py:229-271. If term_len(first) <= first_col - col_spacing, spacing is written on the same line (255-256); otherwise a newline plus indent is written before the description starts (257-259).

query: Among a command's declared parameters, where are the ones flagged as eager moved ahead of the rest, and within each group ordered by the position they were actually supplied on the command line, with parameters never supplied sorted to the end?
why: core.py:138-162. sort_key returns (not item.is_eager, idx) where idx is the parameter's index in invocation_order or infinity if it was never invoked (154-160), and declared parameters are sorted by that key.

query: When a command group lists its subcommands in help output, where are hidden subcommands left out of the listing, and where is the space left for each command's one-line description computed from the longest visible subcommand name?
why: core.py:1894-1920. cmd.hidden entries are skipped when building the commands list (1904-1905); limit is derived as formatter.width - 6 - max(len(name) for name, cmd in commands) (1910-1911) and passed to get_short_help_str.

query: Where is a previously styled piece of text stripped of its embedded terminal color and formatting escape codes, leaving only the plain characters?
why: termui.py:709-718. Delegates directly to strip_ansi(text), removing the escape sequences that style() had inserted.

query: Where is a color value turned into the numeric part of an ANSI escape code, branching on whether it's a named color, an 8-bit palette index, or an RGB triple, and shifted by an offset when it targets the background rather than the foreground?
why: termui.py:569-577. An int becomes a 256-color sequence (570-571), a tuple/list becomes an RGB sequence (573-575), and anything else is looked up by name in _ansi_colors plus offset (577); offset is 10 for background calls.

query: When a usage error is printed, where is the longest of the configured help-flag spellings chosen for the 'try ... for help' hint line?
why: exceptions.py:87-111. help_names is fetched from get_help_option_names and max(help_names, key=len) (99-102) is used so a longer spelling like '--help' is preferred over '-h' in the printed hint.

query: When an option name typed by the user isn't recognized, where are similarly spelled valid option names looked up right away with fuzzy string matching, so a 'did you mean' suggestion is ready before the message is ever shown?
why: exceptions.py:241-260. In __init__, if possibilities were passed, difflib.get_close_matches(option_name, possibilities) is computed eagerly and stored on self.possibilities (254-259) for format_message to use later.

query: When a function is turned into a command without an explicit name, where is the function's name lowercased, its underscores swapped for dashes, and a trailing suffix like '_group' or '_cmd' stripped off to produce the command's name?
why: decorators.py:168-255, specifically 241-246: cmd_name = f.__name__.lower().replace('_','-'); it is rpartitioned on '-' and the suffix dropped if it's one of {'command','cmd','group','grp'}.

query: In the test runner, when a simulated program exits with a status that isn't a plain integer, where is that value written into the captured output and the recorded exit code normalized to 1?
why: testing.py:596-739, specifically 692-703: e_code defaults to 0 if None, and if it isn't an int, its string form is written to stdout followed by a newline and e_code is forced to 1 before becoming exit_code.

query: When deciding what program name to show in help text, where is the choice made between just the script's file name versus a 'python -m module' style name, based on inspecting how the running process's main module looks like it was launched?
why: utils.py:549-601. If __package__ on the __main__ module is None/empty (with a Windows .exe carve-out), it returns just the basename of the executed path (582-589); otherwise it builds 'python -m <package>[.<name>]' from __package__ (591-601).
